summary: The whole board is one generic top-level emu module with no modules for the board's own chips or blocks. Rendering is done by per-line state machines that draw text, then fg, then bg, then sprites into BRAM line buffers. A priority cascade then recreates MAME's screen_update layer order, including MAME's guessed sprite-colour (<4) priority split. Nothing in the code points to schematic-level structure: there are no board net names, PROM priority or board-specific counter chains. Some details are not taken from MAME (forward sprite order, an x==0xFF skip, 9-bit coordinates used without MAME's signed conversion), but they look like FPGA-engineer choices, not hardware derivation.

findings.signal: priority cascade reproduces MAME draw order and pmask guess
findings.note: Overwrite order bg -> sprites with colour>=4 -> fg -> sprites with colour<4 -> tx is exactly MAME's tilemap draw order plus its GFX_PMASK_2 rule for color<0x4 (which MAME marks 'correct?'). It is not a PROM or PAL priority.

findings.signal: decomposition by MAME layers, no chip modules
findings.note: The only video logic is two inline state machines split along MAME's tx/fg/bg tilemaps plus draw_sprites. There is no module for any custom or board video block, and layer names follow MAME's (tx, fg, bg).

findings.signal: tile attribute decode in MAME's tileinfo terms
findings.note: The code uses code=attr[10:0], flip=attr[11] (flip Y for fg, flip X for bg) and colour=attr[15:12], the same field split as MAME's tile_info callbacks (attr & 0x7ff, & 0x800, >> 12).
The control-invert select is named m_invert_ctrl_cs. The C++ 'm_' member prefix comes from MAME's m_invert_controls, which suggests the decode was written from the driver, not from board nets.

findings.signal: address decode as MAME address-map ranges
findings.note: Each select is a start/end range compare that copies MAME's map entries one-for-one, with handler-style names (fg_scroll_y_cs, flip_cs, sound_latch_cs), not decoder chips or PAL equations. It omits the coin-counter writes, as a straight copy of the map minus the bookkeeping handlers would.
Parameterised h/v counters with comparator-set blanking and sync (HTOTAL 383, user offsets). This is generic FPGA timing, not the board's counter chain, and it carries no H/V bit naming.
Double-banked BRAM line buffers indexed by vc[0], with waits on ROM valid signals. This is standard FPGA engineering.

findings.signal: sprite loop diverges from MAME in details
findings.note: The core walks sprites 0..256 forward (MAME goes 1020 down to 0), skips x==0xFF, and compares 9-bit Y directly without MAME's sign conversion. These differ from MAME but follow no visible hardware structure.
Input port addresses, DSW1 bit 7 as VBLANK, the invert-controls XOR and the sound latch with NMI are things any correct core must share with the emulator.
The IPL2 interrupt is raised on the VBL rising edge and cleared on IACK or VBL fall. This is ordinary FPGA glue with no board-specific interrupt circuit.
